Add information derived from Danish CPR numbers

Source: R/add_cpr_info.R
add_cpr_info.Rd

Add selected CPR information without changing the original CPR column.

Usage

add_cpr_info(data, cpr_col, ..., overwrite = FALSE)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble.

cpr_col

CPR column, unquoted or a literal column-name string.

...

Information to add: bday, sex, valid, mod11, age, or age() with a reference year or date. Name a selection to choose its output column, e.g. birth_date = bday. With no selections, adds bday, age, sex, mod11, and valid. Bare age uses today's date.

overwrite

Allow replacing existing output columns? Default FALSE. The CPR source column cannot be replaced.

Value

The input data frame with selected columns added in selection order.

Details

bday is a Date; age is completed calendar years (integer); sex is integer 1 for an odd final digit (male), 0 for even (female). valid checks ten digits and a real encoded calendar date, not whether the number was assigned to a person. Missing and malformed CPRs give valid = FALSE and missing birth date, age, and sex. mod11 is a separate logical checksum, not a requirement for valid. Malformed formats give a missing checksum.

CPR values are cleaned internally with clean_cpr(). To also standardise the source column, use dplyr::mutate(pnr = clean_cpr(pnr)) explicitly. Rows, row order, and input columns are preserved unless overwrite = TRUE. Duplicate output names are always an error.

CPR parsing, calendar validation, and requested outputs share a single native pass. Multiple age selections reuse the decoded birth date. Pre-cleaning is optional: use clean_cpr() when the source column itself must be standardised for joins or export.

For 29 February births, age advances on 1 March in non-leap years. A reference before birth gives a negative age. Use an explicit reference for reproducible analysis; today's date changes between runs.

This selection API replaces add, ref_date, year, and at arguments: use age(year, "primo") or age(date = reference_date) instead. Unlike the previous API, the source CPR column is preserved.

See also

age(), clean_cpr()

Examples

df <- data.frame(pnr = c("0101004007", "111111-1118"), year = 2024:2025)
add_cpr_info(df, pnr)
#>           pnr year       bday age sex mod11 valid
#> 1  0101004007 2024 2000-01-01  26   1  TRUE  TRUE
#> 2 111111-1118 2025 1911-11-11 114   0  TRUE  TRUE
add_cpr_info(df, pnr, sex, birth_date = bday)
#>           pnr year sex birth_date
#> 1  0101004007 2024   1 2000-01-01
#> 2 111111-1118 2025   0 1911-11-11
add_cpr_info(df, pnr,
  primoalder = age(year), ultimoalder = age(year, "ultimo"), sex)
#>           pnr year primoalder ultimoalder sex
#> 1  0101004007 2024         23          24   1
#> 2 111111-1118 2025        113         114   0
add_cpr_info(df, pnr, alder = age(date = "2025-07-01"))
#>           pnr year alder
#> 1  0101004007 2024    25
#> 2 111111-1118 2025   113
